rewrites.blindSummary:
Every province in the country sits under the same intensifying national framework. A leaked omnibus draft law (October 2025) would criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy — up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and 4 years for same-sex ceremonies — and would raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the national medical association objected. A national LGBTI+ rights monitoring group's 2025 human-rights report (published February 2026) finds hostility became explicit national policy in 2025 — centred on the national leadership, implemented through the family ministry — documenting 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment cases (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5-fold), counted from media coverage because the government keeps no hate-crime statistics.

No province-specific ordinance, incident series or court decision concerning trans visitors in this province was documented in this research pass; the national framework above is the whole documented picture for this province. The absence of recorded provincial enforcement is not evidence of local tolerance, and equally not evidence of a local ban.

The report also records that three draft law packages targeting LGBTI people were made public during 2025 - an unprecedented assault that would criminalize expression of LGBTI identities and consensual same-sex relations and make legal gender recognition nearly impossible - but they were ultimately not submitted to parliament.
